scope: Checked records inside callbacks cross C, C++ and CPAN packages through the callable graph carrier: host replies need a typed record recovery, closure arguments run the exact record constructor with nested checked fields first, Lean-produced records cross as payload-only generated records, other native hosts stay refused at projection time, and independent C11/GMP, C++20 and Perl consumers with closed CI checkers prove it.

edits.current:
A checked record follows the same two directions. When a host callback replies
with a checked record such as `Interval`, the descriptor's typed `recovery`
points at an initialized generated record carrying only payload fields; the
wrapper validates and copies it before Lean or the callback runs, and Lean
applies the selected record constructor to the actual reply, running a checked
payload field's own constructor first (for `Weighted`, the `Positive` weight
before `mkWeighted`). A reply that fails either constructor returns
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, counts the one callback invocation, preserves the output
and leaves later calls usable. A checked record Lean produces for the host,
whether a callback argument or a returned closure's result, crosses as the
same generated record without proof fields. A returned Lean closure runs the
selected constructors on its checked-record arguments before its body, and a
record inside `Option`, `Array` or `Except` keeps the direction of its site.
The generated README and the `callback-checked-record-native` workflow
describe the installed C and C++ acceptance; other native hosts still refuse
checked records in callbacks at projection time.

A checked record uses the same `with_recovery(callback, value)` wrapper when a
host callback replies with one: the recovery is the generated value record
with payload fields only, for example `Interval{lo, hi}`, and it is validated
before Lean or the callback runs. Lean applies the selected record constructor
to the actual reply, a checked payload field's own constructor first, and a
reply that fails either constructor throws `Error` with
`STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` after exactly one callback invocation while leaving
later calls usable. Records Lean produces for the host, as callback arguments
or returned-closure results, are the same value records without proof fields.
A returned Lean closure constructs its checked-record arguments before its
body runs, and records inside `std::optional`, `std::vector` or the generated
result type keep the direction of their site. The
`callback-checked-record-native` workflow describes the installed acceptance.

A host callback that replies with a checked record uses the same
`Runtime::Callback` wrapper with a generated record as its recovery, for
example `Interval->new(lo => ..., hi => ...)` carrying payload fields only.
The adapter validates and copies the recovery before Lean or the CODE
reference runs; Lean then applies the selected record constructor to the
actual reply, a checked payload field's own constructor first. A reply that
fails either constructor dies after exactly one callback invocation and leaves
later calls usable. Records Lean produces for the host, as callback arguments
or returned-closure results, are the same generated objects without proof
fields; a returned Lean closure constructs its checked-record arguments before
its body runs, and records inside `Some`, array references or `Ok` keep the
direction of their site. The `callback-checked-record-perl` workflow describes
the installed acceptance on all four pinned interpreters.

## Checked records in native callback packages

Run the C and C++ callback checked-record acceptance on a Linux x64 host with
the pinned Lean toolchain, a C11/C++20 compiler and the GMP development
dependencies:

```sh
source scripts/env.sh
LEAN_BRIDGE_CALLBACK_CHECKED_RECORD_NATIVE_PROFILES=c,cpp \
  node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/callback-checked-record-native-installed.test.mjs
```

The test builds ordinary-source and independently reviewed packages from the
`CallbackCheckedRecords` fixture, verifies the package-set receipt, deletes each
author root, installs from the copied handoff and runs independent C11/GMP and
C++20 consumers. It checks typed record recovery for host replies, invalid
recovery before callback entry, record and nested Subtype field constructor
rejection after callback entry, mixed arguments, returned-closure record
argument rejection, proof-free Lean-produced records in both directions,
unchanged outputs, disposal and reuse after failure. The default record is
`build/callback-checked-records/native.json`. The static generator checks in
`tests/callback-checked-record-native.test.mjs` compile the generated C and
C++ adapters and parse the generated XS without Lean headers.

Run the complete CPAN matrix only after preparing all four pinned interpreters:

```sh
source scripts/env.sh
LEAN_BRIDGE_CALLBACK_CHECKED_RECORD_PERL_TEST=1 \
  node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/callback-checked-record-perl-installed.test.mjs
```

This runs ordinary and reviewed packages on threaded and unthreaded Perl 5.36.3
and 5.38.2, through both prebuilt-only and local XS installation. All sixteen
cells delete author inputs, install offline, relocate the installed tree, remove
the handoff, execute twice and verify every installed-file hash. The consumer
adds `Except (Option Interval)` host replies and `Array (Option Interval)`
closure inputs, exception identity and idempotent close, and reports exact
check, call and rejection counts. The default record is
`build/callback-checked-records/perl.json`.

The hosted workflows run `scripts/run-callback-checked-record-native-ci.sh` and
`scripts/run-callback-checked-record-perl-ci.sh`. They refuse environment
variables that would narrow the matrix, pin the release glibc floor, keep the
original TAP and report, and verify both with the closed checkers in
`scripts/check-callback-checked-record-native-ci.mjs` and
`scripts/check-callback-checked-record-perl-ci.mjs`.

* Select the callable-graph carrier when an erased Subtype or a checked record
 * sits inside a callback signature, even if every erased payload is otherwise
 * acyclic. The primitive native model predates directional callback
 * constructors and cannot represent their recovery protocol; a checked record
 * crosses a callback only as the erased payload mirror that carrier generates,
 * whether the site names its constructor or Lean produces the record bare.
